# Adjudication Task — Chapter 564

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃564화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|회사가 성장하면 가장 먼저 해야 할 것은 무엇인가.
  6|
  7|사람에 따라 각자의 대답은 다르겠지만, CEO라면 누구나 가슴 한구석에 간직한 꿈이 있다.
  8|
  9|바로 사옥 건축이다.
 10|
 11|‘아니, 이 경우에는 증축이라고 해야 하나?’
 12|
 13|길드 하우스 내부를 걷고 있던 나는, 문득 걸음을 멈추고 복도 아래에서 펼쳐지는 광경을 내려다보았다.
 14|
 15|“거, 여기 중력 마법으로 자재 좀 올려 줘요!”
 16|
 17|“자자, 주목. 탱커 출신 손.”
 18|
 19|“저요.”
 20|
 21|“여기도 있습니다. 그런데 왜요?”
 22|
 23|“왜긴, 일 시키려고 그러지. 알아들었으면 이쪽으로 F급 다섯만 붙어. E급도 한두 명 끼워서.”
 24|
 25|드드득. 쿵!
 26|
 27|반질반질한 대리석이 허공을 오르내리고, 근육질의 거한들이 오함마를 휘두를 때마다 단단한 콘크리트 벽이 박살 난다.
 28|
 29|부지런히 움직이는 백여 명의 인부들. 다들 각성자 출신이라 그런지 작업 속도가 장난 아니다.
 30|
 31|물론 그만큼 급여도 비쌌지만, 주머니 두둑한 어느 젊은 대부호에게는 푼돈이나 다름없었다.
 32|
 33|
 34|
 35|‘사람이 많아지니, 길드 하우스가 좁아졌네요.’
 36|
 37|
 38|
 39|며칠 전 그 한마디를 툭 던진 최 팀장은 즉각 행동에 나섰다.
 40|
 41|듣기로는 인근 부지를 웃돈까지 줘 가며 전부 매입해서 대대적인 중축에 착수했다고 하는데, 나야 뭐 그러려니 할 뿐이다.
 42|
 43|‘어차피 내 돈 들어가는 것도 아니고.’
 44|
 45|그리고 내 돈이 들어갈 구석은 따로 있다.
 46|
 47|세금 한 푼 떼지 않은 50조의 자산은 용도에 따라 조금씩 줄어들고 있지만, 남은 돈에 비하면 새 발의 피에 불과하다.
 48|
 49|‘50조라니…….’
 50|
 51|다시 한번 생각해도 비현실적인 액수다. 마치 복도 너머에서부터 점점 가까워지는 한 사람의 모습처럼.
 52|
 53|스으윽.
 54|
 55|유령처럼 허공을 미끄러져 온 거구의 사내가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 56|
 57|「헤이, 기자회견 잘 봤어.」
 58|
 59|“……?”
 60|
 61|아니, 형이 거기서 왜 나와.
 62|
 63|황당한 눈빛으로 매직 존슨을 바라보던 나는 간신히 입을 뗐다.
 64|
 65|“뭡니까?”
 66|
 67|「왜?」
 68|
 69|“왜냐뇨. 그건 제가 드리고 싶은 말씀인데요. 왜 오늘도 여기 계세요?”
 70|
 71|「잠깐 볼일이 있어서.」
 72|
 73|“화장실 때문에 온 건 아니죠?”
 74|
 75|「당연히 아니지. 최에게 전달해 줄 게 있어서 왔어. 겸사겸사 진도 보고.」
 76|
 77|“이메일은 시리얼에 넣어서 먹습니까?”
 78|
 79|「설마 내가 있어서 불편한 건 아니지?」
 80|
 81|“설마 아니라고 생각하신 건 아니죠?”
 82|
 83|칼 같이 받아치는 대답에 매직 존슨이 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
 84|
 85|「헤이, 진. 나처럼 여린 사람은 그렇게 심한 말을 들으면 상처 입는다고.」
 86|
 87|“……상처요?”
 88|
 89|나는 그의 두꺼운 목과 강철같은 구릿빛 팔뚝을 바라보며 생각했다.
 90|
 91|‘칼도 안 들어가게 생겼는데.’
 92|
 93|흑형 근질 보소.
 94|
 95|저 정도 피지컬이라면 지금 당장 마법사에서 근접 헌터로 이직해도 된다.
 96|
 97|심지어 그냥 하는 말이 아닌 것이, 당장 인터넷에 ‘매직 존슨 스태프’를 검색해도 관련 영상이 주르륵 뜬다.
 98|
 99|마법 쓰라고 만든 스태프로 오우거 골통을 일격에 빠갰다는 이야기는 이미 모르는 사람이 없을 정도이며, 헬스 커뮤니티에서는 도대체 저 스태프 중량이 어느 정도인지 의견이 분분할 지경이다.
100|
101|‘그런 인간이 여리긴 개뿔이.’
102|
103|내 그윽한 눈빛에 담긴 뜻을 알아챈 매직 존슨이 고개를 절레절레 내저었다.
104|
105|「몸이 아니라 마음. 마음이 중요한 거야, 진.」
106|
107|“마음이 여린 사람은 대격변을 버티지도 못해요. 강하니까 지금까지 살아남아서 영웅으로 불리는 거죠.”
108|
109|「흐음. 칭찬인지 욕인지 헷갈리는데.」
110|
111|“칭찬이라고 생각하세요.”
112|
113|수상쩍다는 눈빛을 흘린 매직 존슨이 말을 이었다.
114|
115|「어쨌든, 기자회견 잘 봤어. 상당히 의미심장하던걸.」
116|
117|기자회견이라…….
118|
119|나는 민망함에 뒤통수를 긁적였다.
120|
121|대통령의 부탁으로 함께한 청와대 공식 기자회견은 엄청난 반향을 불러왔다.
122|
123|듣기로는 국내 시청률만 70%를 돌파하고 외신에서도 크게 화제가 되었다던가.
124|
125|이틀이 지난 지금도 관련 검색어가 실시간 검색어 상위권을 굳건히 지키고 있을 정도다. 그리고 아마 일주일 뒤에도 마찬가지겠지.
126|
127|“방송 사고의 영향도 있고, 시청률이 좀 잘 나오긴 했죠. 존슨도 봤을 줄은 몰랐네요.”
128|
129|「진의 행보는 미국에서도 늘 화제니까. 특히 몇몇 사람들에게는 프레지던트 백의 마지막 말이 의미심장하게 들렸을 거야. 물론 나도 그중 하나고.」
130|
131|“아, 그거요.”
132|
133|「미스터 리를 왜 그렇게 띄워 주나 했더니, 한 방 제대로 먹였군. 안 그래?」
134|
135|“뭐. 제가 먹인 건 아니긴 한데…… 석고준 입장에서는 꼴 좀 받긴 했겠죠.”
136|
137|지금이 춘추 전국시대는 아니지만, 그래도 거대한 집단을 물려받기 위해 정통성은 언제나 필요하다.
138|
139|그리고 그런 측면에서 보자면 아레스 길드의 새로운 부길드장으로 취임한 석고준은 상당히 정통성이 떨어지는 편이었다.
140|
141|「아레스 길드는 거대한 제국이야. 유언장에 따라 지분을 물려받았다 해도 미스터 리의 영향력까지 전부 이어받지는 못하지. 같은 핏줄이라면 아시아의 정서상 어느 정도 조건은 갖췄겠지만, 그것도 아니잖아?」
142|
143|“이정룡 슬하에 아들이 있긴 했는데, 일찍 요절했다고 하더라고요. 각성하지 않은 일반인이라 지금까지 살아 있더라도 이정룡의 뒤를 잇지는 못했겠지만.”
144|
145|현대의 길드는 무림 문파와 같다. 백면서생이 화산파 장문인이 될 수 없는 것처럼, 헌터로서의 힘과 권위를 지닌 이들이 길드장이 될 수 있는 것이다.
146|
147|그 사실을 모를 리 없는 매직 존슨이 고개를 끄덕였다.
148|
149|「맞는 말이지. 반면에 썩코춘 그 친구는 인격적인 결함과는 반대로 실력 하나는 좋으니까. 이번에 S급 헌터 자격 심사도 엄청난 점수로 통과했다더군. 물론 요즘 연달아 터지는 다른 이슈들 때문에 금방 묻히긴 했지만 말이야.」
150|
151|“썩코춘이 아니라 석고준이요. 그리고 뭐, 그 자식은 어쨌든 이정룡 경호팀장이었잖아요.”
152|
153|「그 정도로는 턱없이 부족해. 지금의 아레스 길드를 있게 만든 또 다른 개국 공신들의 지지가 필요하지. 하지만…….」
154|
155|“시간이 부족했죠.”
156|
157|「맞아. 시간. 아마 미스터 리는 만일의 상황을 대비해 유언장을 작성하면서도 자신이 그리 쉽게 죽을 거라곤 생각 못 했겠지.」
158|
159|하지만 그는 결국 죽었고, 석고준은 후계자의 위치를 공고히 다지기도 전에 왕관을 물려받았다.
160|
161|경호팀장이라는 직책은 최측근이었다는 증거지만, 아레스 길드라는 거대 집단을 모두 물려받기에는 여러 가지 애로사항이 많았다.
162|
163|이정룡의 유언장이 있다고는 해도 나이 지긋한 원로들이 30대의 새파란 청년을 상관으로 깍듯하게 모시기란 쉽지 않다.
164|
165|더군다나 석고준조차 이정룡 사후부터 급격히 무너진 모습을 보인 상황.
166|
167|‘그런 와중에 시청률 70%짜리 청와대 공식 기자회견에서 대놓고 정통성을 부정당했으니…….’
168|
169|백한성 대통령이 던진 한마디는 교묘하면서도 날카로웠다.
170|
171|이번 변이 게이트에 관련된 아레스 길드를 돌려 깎기 식으로 비판함과 동시에, 이정룡의 생전 업적을 띄우며 내가 그의 유지를 잇는다고 포장해 버린 것이다.
172|
173|‘완전히 짜고 치는 판이었지.’
174|
175|이번 기자회견은 국회의원 시절부터 반(反) 아레스 성향을 띠고 있던 백한성 대통령과 최 팀장의 합작품이었다.
176|
177|기자들을 포섭하고, 질문지를 던져 준 다음 원하는 방향으로 이야기를 이끈 것이다.
178|
179|처음부터 끝까지 철저하게 준비된 대사와 배우.
180|
181|만약 이정룡이 살아 있었다면 이번 시나리오는 폐기되었겠지만, 석고준에게는 새로운 언더독(Underdog)의 반란을 잠재울 만한 힘이 없었고 덕분에 우리는 무사히 촬영을 끝마쳤다.
182|
183|국내 시청률 70%라는 훌륭한 흥행 성적과 외신의 스포트라이트를 한껏 받으며.
184|
185|「어쨌든 또 한 번의 작은 승리로군. 이럴 때 샴페인이라도 한잔해야 하는데. 최는 어디 있지?」
186|
187|“전에도 그랬지만, 요즘은 특히 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바쁘죠. 운 좋으면 지금쯤 본인 사무실에 있을 수도 있겠네요.”
188|
189|「없어.」
190|
191|매직 존슨이 어깨를 으쓱하며 덧붙였다.
192|
193|「지금 막 들렀다 오는 길이거든.」
194|
195|“아하. 무슨 일이 또 생기신 모양이네.”
196|
197|새삼스러운 일도 아니다. 말이 팀장이지, 처음부터 최 팀장은 실질적인 길드장이나 다름없었고 지금에 이르러서는 세간의 인식도 그랬다.
198|
199|아마 지금의 그는 대한민국을 통틀어 가장 바쁜 사람 중 하나일 것이다.
200|
201|「헤이, 진. 같이 좀 걸을까?」
202|
203|“좋죠. 으슥한 곳만 피하면요.”
204|
205|「농담이 늘었군.」
206|
207|“…….”
208|
209|「……농담이라고 해 줘.」
210|
211|나는 말 없이 걷는 속도를 올렸다. 부유하듯 허공을 밟으며 뒤따라온 매직 존슨이 투덜거렸다.
212|
213|「진, 왜 자꾸 날 이상한 사람으로 만드는 거야?」
214|
215|“자꾸 이상한 말씀을 하시니까 그렇죠.”
216|
217|「그거야 당연히 장난이지. 그리고 나도 취향이라는 게 있는 사람이야. 진은 해당 사항 없다고. 저기 저 친구라면 모를까.」
218|
219|매직 존슨의 시선을 따라간 곳에는, 훤칠하게 잘생긴 남자가 지나가고 있었다.
220|
221|「못 보던 얼굴인데. 이번에 새로 들어온 길드원인가?」
222|
223|“……누가 들으면 존슨도 우리 길드원인 줄 알겠어요. 아는 얼굴이 몇이나 된다고.”
224|
225|「말도 안 되는 소리! 내가 저런 미남을 기억 못 할 리가 없지!」
226|
227|“…….”
228|
229|쓸데없이 단호한 거 뭔데.
230|
231|이 방면으로는 귀신이네, 진짜. 작게 한숨을 내쉰 내가 대답했다.
232|
233|“저도 이름은 잘 모르는데, 신입은 맞아요. 아마 C급이랬나?”
234|
235|「전 길드장이 누군지는 모르겠지만 피눈물을 흘렸겠군. 저 정도 외모면 화제성도 충분한데. 스타 헌터로도 잘나갈걸?」
236|
237|“말씀하신 전 길드장은 다른 일 때문에 피눈물 흘리고 있을걸요. 기자회견 때 워낙 개망신을 당해서.”
238|
239|「아, 그럼 혹시?」
240|
241|“예. 저 친구, 아레스 길드 소속이었어요.”
242|
243|아레스 길드를 나와 평화 길드로 옮겼다는 것은, 단순히 이적을 의미하는 것이 아니다.
244|
245|대강의 상황을 짐작한 매직 존슨이 중얼거렸다.
246|
247|「철옹성이 흔들리고 있다는 산증인이군. 지금까지 아레스에서 몇 명이나 옮겼지?」
248|
249|“숫자는 적어요. 열 명 남짓.”
250|
251|「숫자가 중요한 게 아니지. 틈이 벌어지고 있다는 증거니까.」
252|
253|나는 작게 고개를 끄덕였다. 외부의 시선으로 보일 정도라면 내부에서는 더 큰 균열이 일어나고 있을 것이다.
254|

The official Blue House press conference I’d attended at the President’s request had caused an enormous stir. I’d heard domestic viewership had topped seventy percent, and it had made headlines abroad too.

[P58]
Even two days later, related searches were holding firm near the top of the real-time rankings. They’d probably still be there a week from now.

[P59]
“The broadcast mishap probably helped, and the ratings were pretty good. I didn’t know you watched it, Johnson.”

[P60]
“What you’re up to is always news in the United States, Jin. President Baek’s final words must have meant a great deal to certain people. Me included.”

[P61]
“Oh, that.”

[P62]
“I wondered why he was praising Mr. Lee so much. Then he landed one hell of a blow, didn’t he?”

[P63]
“Well, I wasn’t the one who landed it… But I bet it got under Go Jun’s skin.”

[P64]
We weren’t living in the Warring States period, but anyone inheriting an organization that big still needed legitimacy.

[P65]
And Go Jun, the new Vice Guild Master of Ares Guild, didn’t have much of it.

[P66]
“Ares Guild is an empire. He may have inherited the shares under Mr. Lee’s will, but that doesn’t mean he inherited all of Mr. Lee’s influence. If he were family, that would count for something in Asian society. But he isn’t, is he?”

[P67]
“Lee Jungryong did have a son, but I heard he died young. He was an ordinary person who never Awakened, though, so he couldn’t have succeeded Lee even if he were still alive.”

[P68]
Modern Guilds were like Murim sects. A bookish scholar couldn’t become the Sect Leader of Huashan; a Guild Master needed the power and authority of a Hunter.

[P69]
Magic Johnson knew that as well as anyone. He nodded.

[P70]
“True. Sseokkochoon, on the other hand, has the skill, whatever his faults as a person. I heard he passed the S-rank Hunter qualification assessment with an incredible score. The news got buried almost immediately under everything else that’s been happening, of course.”

[P71]
“It’s Go Jun, not Sseokkochoon. And the bastard was Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security, at least.”

[P72]
“That’s nowhere near enough. He needs the support of the other people who helped build Ares Guild into what it is. But…”

[P73]
“He didn’t have time.”

[P74]
“Exactly. Time. Mr. Lee probably wrote that will to prepare for the worst without ever imagining he’d die so easily.”

[P75]
But he had died, and Go Jun had inherited the crown before he could establish himself as the successor.

[P76]
The Head of Security title proved he’d been one of Lee Jungryong’s closest aides. Inheriting an organization as vast as Ares Guild was another matter.

[P77]
Even with Lee Jungryong’s will, the elderly veterans weren’t going to find it easy to treat a man in his thirties as their superior. Especially when Go Jun himself had visibly begun to fall apart after Lee’s death.

[P78]
*And then his legitimacy was openly challenged at an official Blue House press conference watched by seventy percent of the country…*

[P79]
President Baek Hanseong’s remark had been subtle and sharp. He’d criticized Ares Guild’s handling of the Mutated Gate without naming it directly, praised Lee Jungryong’s achievements, and presented me as the man carrying on Lee’s wishes.

[P80]
*The whole thing was staged.*

[P81]
The press conference was a joint production by President Baek, who had opposed Ares Guild since his days as a lawmaker, and Team Leader Choi.

[P82]
They’d won over reporters, fed them questions, and steered the conversation where they wanted it to go. The script and cast had been prepared from start to finish.

[P83]
If Lee Jungryong had still been alive, they would have scrapped the plan. But Go Jun lacked the power to put down the new underdog’s rebellion, so we finished the shoot without a hitch—with a domestic rating of seventy percent and the foreign press shining its spotlight on us.

[P84]
“Either way, it’s another small victory. We should have a glass of champagne. Where’s Choi?”

[P85]
“He was busy before, but lately he’s been swamped. If we’re lucky, he might be in his office.”

[P86]
“He’s not.”

[P87]
Magic Johnson shrugged.

[P88]
“I just came from there.”

[P89]
“Ah. Something else must have come up.”

[P90]
That was nothing new. Team Leader Choi might have held a team leader’s title, but he’d effectively been the Guild Master from the start. By now, the public saw him that way too.

[P91]
He was probably one of the busiest people in Korea.

[P92]
“Hey, Jin. Want to walk with me?”

[P93]
“Sure. As long as we stay away from secluded spots.”

[P94]
“You’ve gotten funnier.”

[P95]
“…”

[P96]
“…Tell me that was a joke.”

[P97]
I walked faster without answering. Magic Johnson followed, stepping through the air as if he were floating, and grumbled.

[P98]
“Jin, why do you keep making me out to be some kind of weirdo?”

[P99]
“Because you keep saying weird things.”

[P100]
“I’m joking, obviously. Besides, I have preferences. You’re not my type. That guy over there, maybe.”

[P101]
I followed his gaze to a tall, handsome man walking past.

[P102]
“I haven’t seen him before. New Guild member?”

[P103]
“Someone might mistake you for a member of our Guild. How many people here do you even know?”

[P104]
“That’s ridiculous! You think I wouldn’t remember a handsome man like that?”

[P105]
“…”

[P106]
*Why is he so adamant about it?*

[P107]
He had an uncanny eye for this sort of thing. I sighed and answered.

[P108]
“I don’t really know his name, but he is new. C-rank, I think?”

[P109]
“I don’t know who his former Guild Master was, but he must be crying tears of blood. With looks like that, he’d draw plenty of attention. He could do well as a star Hunter.”

[P110]
“His former Guild Master is probably crying blood over something else. He was humiliated at the press conference.”

[P111]
“Oh. Then was he…?”

[P112]
“Yeah. He used to belong to Ares Guild.”

[P113]
Leaving Ares Guild for Peace Guild meant more than a simple transfer. Magic Johnson seemed to understand.

[P114]
“Living proof that the impregnable fortress is starting to shake. How many have come over from Ares so far?”

[P115]
“Not many. Around ten.”

[P116]
“The number isn’t the point. It proves a crack has opened.”

[P117]
I gave a small nod. If outsiders could see the crack, it was probably much bigger on the inside.

[P118]
*Though we can’t rule out the chance that Go Jun deliberately sent a spy.*

[P119]
That was why the newcomers had gone through a thorough screening. I’d heard they would be sent into actual operations gradually.

[P120]
Even with the System, I couldn’t read people’s minds. Team Leader Choi’s intelligence network would be a great help there.

[P121]
“What’s that place?” Magic Johnson asked. “The security looks serious.”

[P122]
I’d been walking in silence, lost in thought. I looked up and saw the titanium-alloy door he was pointing at.

[P123]
“Oh, that? It’s a training room.”

[P124]
“A training room? In there?”

[P125]
“Yeah.”

[P126]
“My goodness. What kind of training room needs security like that?”

[P127]
Magic Johnson gave an incredulous laugh.

[P128]
“Five overlapping spells? I can understand not wanting anyone to watch you train, but isn’t that excessive inside a Guild House?”

[P129]
“Maybe.”

[P130]
I kept my answer short. The room had been prepared for only a handful of people.

[P131]
More specifically…

[P132]
*For people training in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.*

[P133]
I hadn’t even told Magic Johnson about it. Access was limited to Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, Song Song, and Im Kkeokjeong.

[P134]
“Judging by the security, it isn’t open to every Guild member.”

[P135]
I nodded at his observation.

[P136]
“Right. It’s for the Guild’s founding members, including me.”

[P137]
“Hmm. A secret, then. Now you’ve awakened my curiosity as a mage.”

[P138]
“Put it back to sleep.”

[P139]
“That’s cruel. I can’t even take a quick look?”

[P140]
I hesitated, then waved him off.

[P141]
“No. Someone’s inside.”

[P142]
“Who? Choi?”

[P143]
“No.”

[P144]
A sudden bitterness came over me.

[P145]
“Someone who needs to train more desperately than anyone.”

[P146]
“…?”

[P147]
“There is someone like that.”

[P148]
I couldn’t see him now, but I could picture him clearly: a middle-aged Hunter training over and over, sweat pouring off him like rain. He tried harder than anyone to act as though he was fine, even as he willed himself back onto his feet with his spirit brutally crushed.

[P149]
*Maybe it’s time to start that…*

[P150]
The thought that flashed through my mind slowly took shape as Magic Johnson spoke again.

[P151]
“Can’t be helped. Give this to Choi when you see him.”

[P152]
“Huh? Give him what?”

[P153]
“This.”

[P154]
*Swoosh.*

[P155]
A small object slipped inside my clothes on a faint current of qi.

[P156]
I felt the chip and looked up. The Grand Mage’s face had turned grave.

[P157]
“It’s not just Korea and the United States. Magical power readings are soaring all over the world. Up seven percent from last year. That lucky number has never felt so ominous.”

[P158]
“…!”

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). # Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
